action.instructions: Pilot a fixed-wing aircraft through the next numbered rectangular gate, then the remaining gates in order. Avoid the frame and ground. Maximize gates passed. Use the provided physical state and gate geometry, account for momentum and attitude response, start turns early and stop or reverse before overshooting. World +x follows the course, +y is LEFT, +z is UP. Euler pitch positive means nose DOWN and Euler roll negative means bank LEFT. Decisions last the stated duration. Pitch and bank commands execute simultaneously through the same attitude stabilizer. Neither nominal pitch nor wings-level locks altitude or heading. Banking may affect lift and vertical motion. Use all available relevant measurements; any constant-velocity crossing forecast is only an estimate, not a prediction of your next maneuver. The stabilizer has no gate knowledge. You control pitch only. Choose up, down or level. Another JEV simultaneously chooses bank using this same state. Its new choice is unknown to you.
